source.title: The Dilemma of Quantum Neural Networks
source.authors: Yan Qian; Xin-Biao Wang; Yuxuan Du; Xing-Yao Wu; D. Tao

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study applies random labels and measures training accuracy, using the same randomization test and measure on classical networks in quantum synthetic, Wine, and MNIST settings.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports random-label results for QNNs, but those are not standard deep networks. Those results are outside the claim versions and are not catalog rows. Cited results from other studies were excluded.
record.test_reason: The classical-network comparisons repeat the random-label training experiment and measure training accuracy, directly testing V1 in small, capacity-constrained networks and enlarged MLPs.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct about the authors' emphasis on limited quantum-model capacity and poorer real-world performance, but its MNIST statement is incomplete. The original small models fail to fit random MNIST labels; enlarging the classical MLP substantially improves training accuracy with little additional training time. The authors also conclude that regularization offers limited benefits for quantum trainability and quantum noise further weakens learnability.
record.recipe_differences: Random-label training and training accuracy follow the cited randomization-test approach; the study tests quantum models and classical comparison models on quantum synthetic, Wine, and MNIST data.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model scale change the outcome: MLP reaches 90% on quantum synthetic data, MLP++ completely fits that dataset, MLP reaches 100% on Wine, and all tested models remain at random guess on MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: Quantum models have limited random-label fitting capacity: QNNN and QENN reach training accuracies of 0.562 and 0.630, and quantum hardware noise further reduces their capacity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested quantum neural networks have limited ability to memorize random labels, further weakened by simulated device noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Enlarging classical MLPs incurs little additional training time, and Appendix F reports negligible per-iteration runtime growth with model scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing classical MLP capacity can improve random-label fitting with modest runtime growth in these experiments.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says the related code will be released to a GitHub repository but gives no URL
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: The MNIST result is stated only for an extracted subset with 2000 training samples. The paper reports averages over 10 repetitions but gives no uncertainty estimates for these random-label results. It does not state whether training hyperparameters were unchanged from the true-label settings.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded the QNN random-label results in Figure 4 and Appendix D because QNNs are not standard deep networks. No other classical-network random-label results were omitted.

untested.parts: The record does not capture random-label test accuracy. Unchanged training hyperparameters across true-label and random-label runs are not established for the MLPs; Appendix C gives general shared-setting statements but omits MLP optimizer settings. Enlarged MLP results do not establish success with the original smaller architecture.

No comparison establishes the training-time factor for random versus true labels or convergence as label corruption increases. Small runtime growth when enlarging an MLP addresses a different comparison.
No classical-network experiments fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
No sweep over label-corruption fractions measuring perfect training fit and steadily degrading test performance.
No classical-network comparison of random-label fitting with explicit regularization or true-label generalization after removing regularization.
No measurement separating learning shared real-label patterns from subsequent memorization of noisy labels.

missing.what: Add the enlarged MLP's random-label MNIST training result. The prose reports a substantial accuracy increase, contradicting the record's assertion that no additional classical random-label results were omitted. Its exact accuracy and whether it approaches perfect fitting cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied figure text.
missing.locator: Section 3, final paragraph discussing Figure 4(c), purple curve

missing.what: Record random-label test performance separately for the classical models where readable. Figure 4 includes test curves, which bear on V1's chance-test-performance component, but the supplied text does not permit reliable numerical extraction.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied Figure 4 caption broadly states MNIST failure, while the accompanying prose explicitly adds an enlarged-MLP exception. The exception must be preserved. These are finite-run, model-specific results; the enlarged MNIST MLP's exact endpoint is unreadable in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish that the networks also generalize well on true labels in each random-label setting, or that training hyperparameters were unchanged from the true-label setting.
